 The WTA Finals takes place from November 8–15, 2026, at the Indian Wells Tennis Garden in California, with eight singles players and eight doubles teams battling for the prestigious end-of-season titles. For tennis fans in the UK, the tournament is available through Sky Sports, with Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports Main Event providing coverage. The time difference between California and Britain means the matches are scheduled for evening viewing. 
 In the United States, Tennis Channel is the broadcaster for the WTA Finals. Australian viewers can follow the tournament through beIN Sports Australia and Stan Sport. Quick answer
 WTA Finals Indian Wells: Sky Sports in the UK, Tennis Channel in the US and beIN Sports Australia / Stan Sport.

 Venue: Indian Wells Tennis Garden, California.

 Sky Sports is the main option for UK viewers, with coverage of the WTA Finals throughout the eight-day tournament. Streaming options include Sky Go for eligible subscribers and NOW with a suitable Sports Membership. Both are tied to a UK account and detect your location automatically, so they usually stop working the moment you connect from a hotel Wi-Fi or an airport lounge abroad. If you are travelling during the tournament, using a VPN to keep your connection appearing as if it’s in the UK is usually the easiest way to keep watching your own subscription without interruption. The opening session begins at 20:00 UK time on Sunday, November 8, with the same scheduled start time continuing throughout the round-robin stage. For viewers in the United States, Tennis Channel provides coverage of the tournament, with streaming options available through its subscription service and selected television packages.  The UK is currently observing Greenwich Mean Time (GMT), following the clocks changing on Sunday, October 25. The tournament's scheduled 12:00 local start translates to 20:00 UK time, making the WTA Finals particularly accessible for British viewers. Time Match

 The WTA Finals will conclude on Sunday, November 15, when the singles and doubles champions are crowned. WTA Finals Indian Wells: Players and format
 The WTA Finals features eight singles players split into two groups of four, with the top two from each group progressing to the semi-finals. The original field included Elena Rybakina, Aryna Sabalenka, Mirra Andreeva, Coco Gauff, Jessica Pegula, Elina Svitolina, Karolina Muchova and Linda Noskova. However, defending champion Rybakina withdrew before the tournament due to illness, with Marta Kostyuk replacing her. The updated singles groups are: Group 1 Group 2
